They were developed to address the impracticality of providing full rate-distortion curves in publications, allowing researchers to summarize performance differences in a single value [S1].

The claim states that the metrics were developed to address the impracticality of providing full rate-distortion curves in publications, allowing researchers to summarize performance differences in a single value. The evidence explicitly states: 'given the fact that we performed a huge amount of experiments... it quickly became impractical to simply provide the rate-distortion curves. Instead we opted to make use of the Bjøntegaard Delta Peak Signal Noise Ratio [57] (BD-PSNR) metric... The result is a single PSNR value (in dB) that facilitates the objective comparison...' This directly supports the claim that the metrics were used because providing full curves was impractical and that they provide a single value for comparison.

Since the metrics are calculated based on these curves (which consist of data points), the evidence supports the claim that the inputs are rate-distortion data points for reference and test methods.

A metric to quantify rendering quality loss due to compression, calculated as the difference between compressed and uncompressed PSNR values [S2].

The claim states that the metric quantifies rendering quality loss due to compression and is calculated as the difference between compressed and uncompressed PSNR values. Source [S2] explicitly defines this metric as 'The difference in PSNR... indicates the rendering quality loss due to compression' and provides the formula '∆PSNR = PSNRc − PSNRo', where PSNRc is the PSNR after compression and PSNRo is the PSNR before compression. All facts in the claim are directly present in the evidence.

It is computed by first calculating $PSNR_c$ for the compressed model and $PSNR_o$ for the uncompressed model, then subtracting $PSNR_o$ from $PSNR_c$ to obtain $\Delta PSNR = PSNR_c - PSNR_o$ [S2].

The claim states that Delta PSNR is computed by calculating PSNR_c for the compressed model and PSNR_o for the uncompressed model, then subtracting PSNR_o from PSNR_c. Source [S2] explicitly defines the formula as '∆PSNR = PSNRc − PSNRo' and clarifies that 'PSNRc is the PSNR after compression and PSNRo is the PSNR before the compression.' The notes also confirm the steps: compute PSNR_c, compute PSNR_o, and subtract PSNR_o from PSNR_c. All facts in the claim are present and consistent with the evidence.
